recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 17-2-0307, ALL LOTS CLASSIFIED AS RS-3 REQUIRE AN OPEN SPACE BETWEEN MAIN BUILDING AND REAR ACCESSORY STRUCTURE.AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, IT WAS OBSERVED THAT THE REAR ACCESORY STRUCTURE IS RIGHT UP TO THE REAR ENCLOSED PORCH OF THE MAIN BUILDING, NO REAR OPEN YARD SPACE IN BETWEEN WAS OBSERVED.

recent_violations.ordinance: Provide
recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 14A-4-401.1, IT'S UNLAWFUL TO CONSTRUCT, ENLARGE, ALTER, UNLESS A PERMIT FOR SUCH WORK HAS FIRST OBTAINED. AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, AN ACCESSORY METAL STRUCTURE WAS OBSERVED AT THE REAR SET BACK AREA OF THE LOT, MEASURING APPROXIMATELY 30'X56'. THE  FOLLOWING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, WAS OBSERVED IN THE INTERIOR OF THE STRUCTURE, 2 NEW TOILET ROOMS, 1 NEW WARM AIR FURNACE (AT THE TOP OF THE TOILET ROOMS) AND NEW ELECTRICAL FIXTURES AND RECEPTACLES THROUGHOUT.A SUBSEQUENT PERMIT SEARCH WAS CONDUCTED AND PERMIT NUMBER 100939250 THAT WAS ISSUED ON 04/27/2022 WAS FOUND. THIS PERMIT HAS BEEN VOIDED DUE TO THE FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH PERMIT SPECIFICATIONS.A NEW PERMIT IS REQUIRED TO INCLUDE ALL DISCIPLINES INVOLVED IN THE CONSTRUCTION OF SUCH STRUCTURE, IT WAS OBSERVED THAT ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, HVAC AND CARPENTRY/ROOFING WERE DISCIPLES USED IN THE CONSTRUCTION.SUBJECT TO ZONING GUIDELINES AND APPROVAL, A NEW PERMIT IS NOW REQUIRED IN THE REDUCTION OF THE METAL ACCESSORY STRUCTURE ORIGINALLY BUILT WITHOUT A PERMIT.

recent_violations.ordinance: Remove
recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 17-2-0204 & 17-2-0207, LOTS CLASSIFIED AS RS-3 ARE NOT ALLOWED TO BE USED AS A BUSINESS LOCATION.AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT A SEWER AND PLUMBING BUSINESS WAS BEING OPERATED OUT OF THE REAR METAL ACCESSORY STRUCTURE. A SIGN READING "SEWER & DRAIN PLUMBING INC" WAS POSTED IN THE INSIDE OF THE STRUCTURE.A COMMERCIAL GENERATOR AND A TILT TRAILER WITH A BACK HOE EXCAVATOR ON TOP, WERE OBSERVED INSIDE THE REAR METAL ACCESSORY STRUCTURE.

recent_violations.ordinance: Provide
recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 17-9-0201-D, ACCESSORY STRUCTURES MAY NOT OCCUPY MORE THAN 60% OF THE AREA REQUIRED SET BACK.AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION THE REAR METAL ACCESSORY STRUCTURE WAS BUILT UP TO THE SIDE LOT LINES AND FROM THE REAR LOT LINE TO THE REAR ENCLOSED PORCH OF THE MAIN BUILDING, THUS OCCUPIYING 100% OF THE REAR SET BACK AREA.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
